learningObjectives: Explain class hierarchy structure in a scenario.
Explain modular architecture and enterprise reuse in a scenario.
Explain new Pega platform applications in a scenario.

elements.description: Place assets at their reuse scope: enterprise-wide → Organization; regional or brand-wide → optional Division; unit-wide → optional Unit (requires Division); a specific business application → Implementation. Platform supplies the foundation. Constellation starts with the Data Model and generates a prescribed experience; its design system, architecture, DX API and business engine have distinct roles.

elements.text: Worked example: Shared address lookup belongs to a reusable scope; a single-brand returns policy belongs to that brand. Decide who consumes an asset before choosing its layer.

elements.description: Keep Enterprise lean. Put reusable customer data, single-system integration and utility capabilities in modules; place workflow-specific Cases in business applications. Specialize geographic or segment differences in innovation applications. Reuse modules through built-on applications or the wizard. Prefer parameters, extension points and Configuration Sets to copies; shared changes affect consumers.

elements.text: Worked example: A document conversion service can be one utility module consumed by Claims and Lending. Put workflow-specific decisions in the consuming business application.

elements.description: Blueprint captures a collaborative application design: Case Types, lifecycle, data and Personas. App Studio’s New Application wizard turns an existing or newly created Blueprint into an initial application. Treat generated design as a starting point to review against requirements. Reusable designs speed repeated application creation.

elements.text: Worked example: A team agrees a Warranty Blueprint, reviews its Case lifecycle and data, then uses the wizard to create the application. A design import still needs implementation and validation.

elements.title: Close the notes and explain

elements.text: Try the quiz before rereading. Explain why each distractor fails. Use Smart Review on later days; revisit answers you got wrong with high confidence.

examPitfalls.title: Reuse scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A brand policy must be copied into every application.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose the narrowest layer that covers all intended consumers.

examPitfalls.title: Shared changes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A module change cannot affect consumers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Assess shared consumers when changing a reused capability.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint vs deployment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Importing a design completes production deployment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review and implement the generated application, then validate and deploy it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two product teams need the same customer lookup capability. Where should reusable behavior live?

options.text: Separate copies in each Case Type

practiceQuiz.rationale: A shared capability serves both consumers; copies create separate maintenance.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Modular architecture and Enterprise reuse. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Copies duplicate maintenance instead of sharing one capability.
optionExplanations.B: Both teams can consume the same reusable capability.
optionExplanations.C: A personal development scope does not provide the requested shared module.
optionExplanations.D: Operator profiles describe users, not a reusable customer lookup capability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A policy applies to every application in one brand, but not to the entire enterprise. Which optional scope fits?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Division provides the intermediate reuse scope.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Class hierarchy structure. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Platform provides built-in assets, not this brand-specific policy.
optionExplanations.B: A personal development scope is not the shared brand layer.
optionExplanations.C: Division can hold assets shared within one brand.
optionExplanations.D: Separate implementations duplicate a policy shared across the brand.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO choices support modular reuse?

options.text: Put all business workflows in the Enterprise layer
Create an integration module for one external system
Copy every Rule before consuming it
Expose configuration instead of duplicating behavior

practiceQuiz.rationale: A focused capability and configuration keep consumers reusable.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Modular architecture and Enterprise reuse. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Keep Enterprise lightweight; application workflows belong in business applications.
optionExplanations.B: A single-system integration is a reusable module capability.
optionExplanations.C: Copying creates independent maintenance instead of reuse.
optionExplanations.D: Configuration lets consumers adapt shared behavior without copying it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team has an agreed Blueprint and needs an initial Constellation application. What should it use?

options.text: New Application wizard in App Studio

practiceQuiz.rationale: Packaging and skimming operate on existing assets; application creation uses the wizard.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on New Pega Platform applications. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Packaging existing assets does not create the requested application from Blueprint.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset version maintenance is not application creation from Blueprint.
optionExplanations.C: The App Studio wizard creates an initial application from Blueprint.
optionExplanations.D: Circumstancing specializes behavior rather than creating an application from Blueprint.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer enables Unit without Division. Which hierarchy assumption needs correction?

options.text: Unit requires Division to be enabled
Division is mandatory for every application

practiceQuiz.rationale: Unit depends on the optional Division level.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Class hierarchy structure. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Unit is available only when Division is enabled.
optionExplanations.B: Division is optional; Unit depends on enabling it.
optionExplanations.C: Implementation contains application-specific assets; specialization is supported.
optionExplanations.D: Organization contains enterprise-wide assets, including integrations, not only UI.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A regional reimbursement workflow varies while customer data access stays common. Which design fits?

options.text: Move all regional workflows to Platform
Share the data module and specialize the business behavior

practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate the invariant capability from the varying policy.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Modular architecture and Enterprise reuse. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Duplicate integrations split maintenance of unchanged customer access.
optionExplanations.B: Platform is the foundation, not the home for regional workflows.
optionExplanations.C: Personal development scopes do not implement the requested modular architecture.
optionExplanations.D: Reuse common data capabilities and specialize regional business behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO items belong to a Blueprint application design?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint models business design rather than operational artifacts.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on New Pega Platform applications. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint models application design, not Ruleset passwords.
optionExplanations.B: Case lifecycle design is part of the application Blueprint.
optionExplanations.C: Personas describe the application users represented in Blueprint.
optionExplanations.D: Runtime production logs are not application design elements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly connects Constellation to application behavior?

options.text: Its design system replaces the business engine
The Data Model drives a prescribed user experience
It requires hand-coded screens for every property
Its DX API is only a database backup interface

practiceQuiz.rationale: Model-driven configuration is the key relationship; UI and engine retain distinct responsibilities.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Class hierarchy structure. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: UI components and the business logic engine have different responsibilities.
optionExplanations.B: Constellation uses the Data Model to generate a prescribed experience.
optionExplanations.C: Constellation favors configuration and predefined experiences over bespoke screens.
optionExplanations.D: DX API powers user experiences; it is not just backup.

quickRecap.value: Organization → enterprise; Division → brand/region; Unit requires Division; Implementation → specific application.
Shared capability in a module; workflow in business app; situational variation in innovation app.
Design first; review generated Cases, data and Personas; create through the New Application wizard.
